name: git
description: Version-control judgement for work in a repository, and the checkouts themselves: cloning into Brightside's code root, reading a checkout directly, and what needs the owner's word before it happens. Load before asking Claude Code to clone, commit, push, merge or rewrite history.

content.inline:
# Git

Git work happens inside a project, through Claude Code; this is the judgement
you bring to it, and where the repositories live.

## Checkouts

- The `code` file root is where repositories are checked out: one directory
  per repository, each a Claude Code project the owner has declared.
  Brightside's own source is expected at `code/brightside` — a project by
  default, empty until cloned.
- To clone into an empty project, have Claude Code run `git clone <url> .`
  there (a project allowing git commands can). Clone only repositories the
  owner has asked for; a project that already holds a checkout is updated
  with `git pull`, never re-cloned.
- Anything that talks to a remote — clone of a private repository, fetch,
  push — needs a credential, and headless Claude Code cannot type one: it
  fails at once, saying so. The owner signs in once at a terminal of their
  own (the credential manager remembers it); tell them that is the step, and
  never try to supply or embed a credential yourself.
- A checkout is also files: the file tools read it directly — the roots tool
  names the root, list and tree navigate it, read shows a file — so you can
  look at a rulebook, a diff's target or a test without a Claude Code turn.
  Changes to the code go through Claude Code, which builds and tests them.

## Judgement

- The repository's own rules come first: its README, AGENTS.md or
  CONTRIBUTING say which branch is worked on, how commits are written and who
  commits as whom. Have Claude Code read them before the first change.
- Commit as the repository's configured git identity, never as an invented
  name, and keep any attribution lines the repository asks for.
- A commit is one coherent change with a message that says what and why.
  Unrelated changes already in the working tree are left alone and never
  swept into a commit; say when the tree holds work you did not make.
- Review before committing: ask for the diff and the test outcome, and read
  both.
- Local and reversible needs no permission: cloning into its own project,
  branches, commits, stashes, merges into a working branch. Outward-facing or
  hard to undo does: pushing, opening pull requests, tagging releases,
  force-pushing, rewriting or deleting history, resetting away work,
  switching the branch the owner is on. Ask first, every time, and name
  exactly what will happen.
- Never rewrite history that has been shared, and never skip the repository's
  hooks or checks to get a commit through: a failing hook is a problem to fix.
